ai_summary: Great Britain's wind generation currently stands at 3.1 GW, with estimated Scottish wind output contributing 2.0 GW, representing 19.8% of installed Scottish wind capacity. While Scotland maintains an optimal carbon intensity of 0 gCO2/kWh compared to 215 gCO2/kWh GB-wide, transmission constraints severely restrict the transfer of clean energy southward. Consequently, 5,887 MWh of Scottish generation has been curtailed so far today through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring a constraint cost of about £182,521. To compensate for this localized clean energy deficit, downstream thermal plants burned an estimated 1,118,587 m3 of gas elsewhere, releasing an avoidable 2,061 tonnes of CO2 into the atmosphere. Annualizing today's constraint expenditure points to an estimated total yearly cost of £67 million. Across typical UK electricity demand, this ongoing transmission friction adds an estimated £0.22/MWh to everybody's invoice in the UK, highlighting the clear economic and decarbonization case for reinforcing cross-border grid infrastructure.
